title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 57
paragraphs: When all had crossed and had set out on their way, a great portent appeared to them, to which Xerxes paid no attention, though its meaning was easy to guess: a mare gave birth to a hare. The meaning was easy to guess: Xerxes was about to march an army against Greece most proudly and magnificently, but would come running back for his life to the place from which he had started. There had been another portent earlier, while he was still at Sardis: a mule brought forth young, and the offspring was a mule with both male and female genitals, the male above the female. But Xerxes took no notice of either of these portents and went on his way, and the land army with him.
